concepts.name: Artificial neuron and weights
concepts.summary: Explain that a neuron computes a weighted sum of inputs plus a bias and passes it through a nonlinearity.

concepts.name: Layers and network depth
concepts.summary: Describe how stacking input, hidden and output layers lets a network build progressively more abstract features.

concepts.name: Activation functions
concepts.summary: Explain why nonlinear activations such as ReLU, sigmoid and tanh are needed and how their output ranges differ.

concepts.name: Forward pass
concepts.summary: Recall that a forward pass computes layer by layer from input to prediction.

concepts.name: Loss function
concepts.summary: Understand that a loss measures prediction error and that training aims to minimise it, e.g. cross-entropy or mean squared error.

concepts.name: Training by gradient descent
concepts.summary: Understand that weights are repeatedly nudged opposite the gradient of the loss, scaled by a learning rate.

concepts.name: Backpropagation idea
concepts.summary: Describe backpropagation as applying the chain rule backward to get the gradient of the loss for every weight.

misconceptions.text: A neural network with more layers is always more accurate.
Stacking layers without activation functions still gives a more powerful model than a single layer.
Backpropagation is the algorithm that updates the weights.

concepts.name: Mini-batch SGD and epochs
concepts.summary: Train a model with mini-batches, setting batch size and number of epochs and reading the resulting loss curves.

concepts.name: Tensors and autograd
concepts.summary: Use a framework such as PyTorch to build tensors, compute gradients automatically and apply optimiser steps.

concepts.name: Training loop structure
concepts.summary: Write a loop with forward pass, loss, backward pass, optimiser step and gradient reset, plus separate evaluation mode.

concepts.name: Overfitting and validation curves
concepts.summary: Diagnose overfitting from diverging training and validation loss and apply early stopping.

concepts.name: Convolution and pooling layers
concepts.summary: Apply convolutional filters, stride, padding and pooling to image tensors and compute output shapes.

concepts.name: Softmax and cross-entropy
concepts.summary: Turn logits into class probabilities with softmax and train classifiers with cross-entropy loss.

concepts.name: Weight initialisation
concepts.summary: Understand why random, scaled initial weights are needed to break symmetry and keep signals stable.

concepts.name: Using GPUs for training
concepts.summary: Move models and data to a GPU and understand why parallel matrix operations speed training.

misconceptions.text: Training loss going down means the model is getting better in general.
Initialising all weights to zero is a safe default.
Softmax outputs are calibrated probabilities that can be trusted as certainty.

concepts.name: Vanishing and exploding gradients
concepts.summary: Analyse how repeated multiplication through depth shrinks or inflates gradients and choose remedies such as ReLU, init and clipping.

concepts.name: Batch normalisation
concepts.summary: Apply normalisation layers, and handle their different behaviour in training versus evaluation mode.

concepts.name: Dropout and weight decay
concepts.summary: Apply dropout and weight decay to reduce overfitting and tune their strength.

concepts.name: Adaptive optimisers and schedules
concepts.summary: Compare SGD with momentum and Adam, and use learning rate schedules and warmup.

concepts.name: CNN architecture patterns
concepts.summary: Analyse how depth, receptive field and skip connections shape CNN design and trainability.

concepts.name: Transfer learning and fine-tuning
concepts.summary: Reuse a pretrained network by freezing layers or fine-tuning for a new dataset.

concepts.name: Recurrent networks and LSTMs
concepts.summary: Analyse how recurrence and gated memory cells process sequences and mitigate gradient problems.

concepts.name: Data augmentation and pipelines
concepts.summary: Build input pipelines with batching, shuffling and augmentation to improve generalisation.

misconceptions.text: Dropout and batch normalisation behave the same during training and inference.
Adam always outperforms SGD and needs no learning rate tuning.
LSTMs completely eliminate vanishing gradients and long-range dependency problems.

concepts.name: Self-attention mechanism
concepts.summary: Analyse how queries, keys and values yield context-weighted representations and why scaling and softmax matter.

concepts.name: Transformer block design
concepts.summary: Dissect transformer blocks including multi-head attention, feed-forward layers, residuals, normalisation and positional information.

concepts.name: Encoder, decoder and masking
concepts.summary: Distinguish encoder-only, decoder-only and encoder-decoder models and the role of causal and padding masks.

concepts.name: Tokenisation and embeddings
concepts.summary: Analyse how subword tokenisation and learned embeddings represent text for neural models.

concepts.name: Pretraining and fine-tuning paradigms
concepts.summary: Evaluate masked and autoregressive pretraining objectives and adaptation methods such as fine-tuning and parameter-efficient tuning.

concepts.name: Training diagnostics and debugging
concepts.summary: Judge causes of training failure from loss, gradient norms and activations, and verify with sanity checks.

concepts.name: Mixed precision and multi-GPU training
concepts.summary: Analyse memory and throughput tradeoffs of mixed precision, gradient accumulation and data-parallel training.

concepts.name: Model evaluation and ablation
concepts.summary: Evaluate architectural choices with controlled ablations, appropriate metrics and multiple seeds.

misconceptions.text: Self-attention inherently understands word order without positional information.
Transformers are strictly better than CNNs and RNNs on any task and data size.
Attention weights are a faithful explanation of why a model made its prediction.

concepts.name: Scaling laws and compute tradeoffs
concepts.summary: Evaluate how loss scales with parameters, data and compute and decide allocations for a given budget.

concepts.name: Efficient attention and long context
concepts.summary: Judge approaches to reduce quadratic attention cost and memory, including caching and sparse or linear variants.

concepts.name: Generative model families
concepts.summary: Compare autoregressive, latent-variable, adversarial and diffusion generative models by objective, quality and stability.

concepts.name: Novel architecture design
concepts.summary: Design architectures whose inductive biases match a problem's structure, such as equivariance or modality fusion.

concepts.name: Large-scale distributed training
concepts.summary: Design a training setup combining data, tensor and pipeline parallelism and sharding for models that exceed one device.

concepts.name: Generalisation and optimisation theory
concepts.summary: Evaluate explanations for why overparameterised networks generalise, including flat minima and double descent.

concepts.name: Robustness and distribution shift
concepts.summary: Assess model vulnerability to adversarial and shifted inputs and choose mitigations and evaluation protocols.

concepts.name: Alignment and preference tuning
concepts.summary: Create pipelines that adapt pretrained models to human preferences and critique their failure modes.

misconceptions.text: Scaling up model size alone will reliably fix reasoning and robustness failures.
Classical bias-variance reasoning implies overparameterised networks must overfit.
Adversarial robustness comes for free with higher clean accuracy.
